newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Death toll could rise in Lisbon bridge accident.
newsitem.headline: Death toll could rise in Lisbon bridge accident.

text.p: Four or five workers, including two Frenchmen, were missing on Thursday after a metal girder collapsed at a Lisbon bridge project, killing a Portuguese employee and injuring eight other people.
A spokeswoman for the Anglo-French consortium Lusoponte, which is building the bridge over the river Tagus, named the two missing Frenchmen as Etienne Muller and Jerome Cornielle.
The nationality of the other missing men, who were apparently knocked 40 metres (130 feet) from the bridge into the river when the girder broke, was not immediately known.
Amongst the injured was English engineer Anthony Freeman, who was in a coma in a Lisbon hospital. The other seven workmen hurt, all Portuguese, were in less serious condition.

The dead man, named as Vicente Casanova, was the Portuguese foreman in charge of work in that part of the bridge. The spokeswoman said that the fact that he had been killed made it difficult to say exactly how many workers had been in the area at the time of the accident.
Some 3,500 people are employed on building the 18-km (11-mile) bridge which is one of Europe's largest construction projects.
Work around the area where the accident occurred was halted while an official inquiry was carried out into its causes.
